prompt: Menhir derives the canonical self identity for a namespace deterministically (self_uuid_for_namespace) and binds it only through an explicit declaration, instead of treating extracted entities named 'user' as the human. Why not just resolve self by the name 'user'? And is this binding enforced in production today?

points: the name user carries no provenance
activation is an open owner decision

gold_citations.quote: Rejected. Software actors, account concepts, and third-person references legitimately use that
one identity fragmented across the graph.

notes: Answer is written in .agent/adr/0010-deterministic-canonical-self-identity.md at Menhir fdaf56bf (ADR merged in #133, 2026-09-24). Gold points and quotes are verbatim from the ADR; drafted by Claude from the ADR text only, pending owner review.
